content: The academic year consists of two semesters: Fall and Spring.
The Fall semester starts in September.
The Spring semester starts in February.
Each semester has a total duration of 18 weeks.
Each semester includes 16 weeks of teaching.
Each semester includes 2 weeks for examinations and result declaration.
The mid-term examination of theory courses has a weightage of 30%.
The mid-term exam is conducted after 8 weeks of teaching.
The mid-term exam includes objective questions of 10 marks.
The mid-term exam includes short answer questions of 10 marks.
The mid-term exam includes long answer questions of 30 marks.
The total duration of the mid-term exam is 1.5 hours.
The internal assessment of theory courses has a weightage of 20%.
Assignments contribute 5% to internal assessment.
Presentations contribute 5% to internal assessment.
Quizzes and tests contribute 10% to internal assessment.
The final-term examination of theory courses has a weightage of 50%.
The final-term exam is conducted after 16 weeks of teaching.
The final-term exam includes objective questions of 10 marks.
The final-term exam includes short answer questions of 10 marks.
The final-term exam includes long answer questions of 30 marks.
The total duration of the final-term exam is 2 hours.
The mid-term lab exam has a weightage of 30%.
Viva voce contributes 10% in the mid-term lab exam.
Practical performance contributes 20% in the mid-term lab exam.
The duration of the mid-term lab exam is 3 hours.
The internal evaluation of lab courses has a weightage of 20%.
Lab attendance contributes 5% in internal evaluation.
Notebook completion contributes 5% in internal evaluation.
Presentation and demonstration contribute 10% in internal evaluation.
The final-term lab exam has a weightage of 50%.
Viva voce contributes 10% in the final lab exam.
Practical performance contributes 40% in the final lab exam.
The duration of the final lab exam is 3 hours.
A student must obtain at least 50% marks in each paper to pass.
85% and above corresponds to Grade A with GPA 4.0 and Excellent performance.
70 to 84% corresponds to Grade B with GPA between 3.0 and 3.9.
60 to 69% corresponds to Grade C with GPA between 2.0 and 2.9.
50 to 59% corresponds to Grade D with GPA between 1.0 and 1.9.
Marks below 50% correspond to Grade F which means fail.
Grade W indicates a withdrawn course.
Grade I indicates an incomplete course.
SGPA is calculated by dividing the sum of grade points multiplied by credit hours by total credit hours in a semester.
CGPA is calculated by dividing the sum of grade points multiplied by credit hours of all semesters by total credit hours.
If the third decimal in GPA is 5 or more, it is rounded up.
If the third decimal in GPA is 4 or less, it is rounded down.
A withdrawn course is not counted as fail and is not included in GPA or CGPA calculation.
An incomplete course is not included in GPA or CGPA calculation.
Thesis or project evaluation is conducted by an external examiner appointed by the competent authority.
The viva voce of thesis is conducted by the external examiner along with the supervisor and head of department.
Honorarium is paid to examiners including the head of department for thesis evaluation.
